title: Engineers pulse and ops priorities - Oct 05 2026
content:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 10:00–11:00 PT
Location: Zoom + #eng-serving-runtime
Facilitator: Samira Patel
Note taker: Diego Morales
Attendees (partial): Samira, Diego, Priya, Liam, Maya, Jordan, Anu, Harpreet, Clare, Marcus

TL;DR
- Short window outage on 2026-10-02 (region eu-west-1) traced to a cache eviction bug during rollout; patch deployed, postmortem in progress.
- P95 latency for text-generation pipelines improved 8% week-over-week after kernel selection change; but P99 remains high for >1% of requests on long-context flows.
- Autoscaling policy A/B test (scale-granularity) shows 12% cost savings for steady workloads but increases tail latency for spikier traffic — hold final roll.
- Private deployment customer onboarding: two successful VPC installs; follow-up on KV-cache tuning requested.
- Action focus this week: incident RCA, P99 plan for long-context inference, finish kernel selector rollout (canary -> prod), and OBS retention tuning for traces.

1) Incident recap (2026-10-02, 02:13–02:42 UTC)
- Symptom: ~18-minute outage affecting hosted inference in eu-west-1 causing 502s and request timeouts.
- Immediate mitigation: rollback of the canary deployment for kernel-selector v2 and failover to adjacent region for some customers.
- Root cause (preliminary): a race in KV-cache eviction logic combined with a new background rewriter that produced inconsistent cache keys under rare sequence-length transitions. This caused cache lookup failures and amplified request resubmissions, overloading the node-local RPC queue.
- Impact: 17% of requests in that region saw elevated errors, SLA credit being evaluated by Finance/CS.
- Next steps: (a) finish detailed postmortem doc and share with CS/Legal by 2026-10-08; (b) add unit + fuzz tests for cache key normalization (owner: Liam, due 2026-10-09); (c) instrument additional guardrails to drop backoff-resubmission after X retries (owner: Priya, due 2026-10-12).

2) Key metrics and operational health
- Aggregated hosting metrics (last 7d):
  - Token throughput (hosted): 3.2B tokens/day (stable)
  - P50 latency (gpt-like text gen, 512 context): 45ms (–3ms WoW)
  - P95 latency: 230ms (–20ms WoW)
  - P99 latency: 980ms (+90ms WoW) — spike driven by long-context (>2k) requests and some client-side synchronous retries.
  - Error rate: 0.18% (goal <0.1%) — incident bump accounted for 0.07% of that.
  - GPU utilization across Dedicated pools: 63% average, spotty packing on small-instance pools.
- Observability notes: trace retention default (7d) is producing heavy storage pressure; SRE recommends 14d for model-rollouts but with selective sampling. Observability team will propose sampling by route/model (owner: Maya, due 2026-10-13).

3) Rollouts and deployment updates
- Kernel selector rollout v2: Canary showed improved median and P95 on short-context flows; paused after the eu-west incident. Current plan: revert canary in eu-west (done), add KV normalization fixes, expand integration tests, resume canary with lower traffic slice.
- Canary -> prod checklist pending: additional cue-based abort metrics and graceful degradation on cache errors. (owners: Samira + Jordan)
- Dedicated: capacity resize for high-throughput customers scheduled 2026-10-09. Running a short soak test on the new packing algorithm — initial results look promising (reduction in per-token cost by ~6% for steady streams).

4) Deep dive: P99 on long-context flows
- Problem: for requests >2k tokens, latency tail grows superlinearly due to KV-cache misses and patchy attention-kernel path selection.
- Current hypothesis: mixed-precision quantization path triggers slower fallback kernels for some attention patterns; combined with less effective prefix caching for long prompts.
- Proposed mitigations:
  - Add a dedicated long-context kernel path that avoids fallback heuristics (owner: Marcus, prototype by 2026-10-19).
  - Improve prefix/KV caching heuristics to prefer store-on-write for frequently accessed prefixes (owner: Harpreet, experiment by 2026-10-15).
  - Instrument a synthetic workload that mimics large-context few-shot prompts to target regression testing (owner: Clare, due 2026-10-12).

5) Product & customer updates that affect engineering
- CS reported two customers on Dedicated asking for predictable tail latency guarantees for inference >3k tokens. Product asked for a proposal to offer "long-context tier" as an add-on — proposal needed by 2026-10-22 (lead: Samira + Product-hosted-api).
- Private deployments: onboarding for an EU-regulated customer completed (air-gapped option). They requested fine-grained KV-cache control and audit hooks. Solutions Eng to draft config knobs (owner: Diego, due 2026-10-14).

6) Experiments and Optimize findings
- Autoscaling policy A/B (coarse vs fine-grained scaling): coarse scaling reduces oscillation but wastes capacity on spikey traffic; fine-grained saves on steady jobs. Longer test window needed. Decision: keep both policies available as presets; add dynamic policy recommendation based on traffic profile (owner: Priya + Optimize team, spec by 2026-10-18).
- Quantization experiment: int4 path shows good quality for small LMs, but regression on instruction-following metrics for some models. Research to produce model-by-model guidance (owner: Research/Applied-ML, contact: Maya).

7) Cross-team asks and blockers
- Observability: need 2 additional small JVM instances for trace ingestion to unblock 14d retention pilot (ask sent to infra; priority = high).
- Security: review of new KMS rotation flow for Private customers scheduled for 2026-10-11; need SRE and platform leads to attend.
- SRE: request for a standardized chaos-test harness for region failover; platform-engineering to re-use existing infra (owner: Jordan, due 2026-11-01).

8) Decisions made in this meeting
- Pause expanding kernel-selector rollout in regions until KV-cache normalization and new tests land.
- Keep both autoscaling presets and add an automated recommender, not a forced switch.
- Prioritize incident postmortem and follow-up fixes over new perf feature launches for the next sprint.

9) Action items (owner — due date)
- Liam: add unit + fuzz tests for cache key normalization — 2026-10-09
- Priya: implement resubmission guardrail (drop after 3 retries by default) — 2026-10-12
- Marcus: prototype long-context kernel path — 2026-10-19
- Harpreet: KV caching experiment (store-on-write) and traffic experiment plan — 2026-10-15
- Clare: build synthetic long-context regression test harness and include in nightly suite — 2026-10-12
- Diego: draft Private deployment KV-control config options for Solutions Eng — 2026-10-14
- Maya: sampling plan proposal for 14d observability retention — 2026-10-13
- Samira + Product-hosted-api: draft long-context tier pricing/tech spec — 2026-10-22

10) Parking lot / open questions
- How aggressive should we be with automatic rollback thresholds for kernel-selector? (need proposed thresholds from Jordan)
- Do we surface a latency SLO specifically for long-context workloads or treat as an add-on? (decision needed by 2026-10-22)

Notes / Misc
- Quick shoutout: team that shipped the new packing algorithm — small team, big impact. Keep highlighting these wins in weekly syncs.
- Next all-hands deep-dive topic requested: "Model-aware kernel selection and developer ergonomics" — proposed for 2026-10-19.

Meeting adjourned 11:02 PT.
